author: Barrie Linch
text: It's only an estimate. The A1c measures how much glucose has attached to the haemoglobin in your red blood cells over the last 2-3 months. The CGM has no way of taking that measurement so it takes the average of all your readings over that time period and using some really complex calculation, it estimates what your A1c will be when the proper test is done, in the lab. It's no wonder it's not always accurate. In fact, it's a wonder how they get it anywhere near the correct figure!
